name: Levetiracetam
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Levetiracetam is cleared mainly by the kidneys (66% unchanged). The US label reduces the dose by creatinine clearance adjusted for body surface area and, for dialysis patients, gives 500 to 1,000 mg every 24 hours plus a 250 to 500 mg supplement after each hemodialysis, which removes about 50% in 4 hours.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses Cockcroft-Gault CrCl adjusted to body surface area (mL/min/1.73 m2): >80, 50–80, 30–50, <30, and ESRD on dialysis. Site bands keep this measure; label cut-offs inside a band are stated.
chip: Dose by CrCl; supplement after HD

bands.recommendation: CrCl >80: 500 to 1,500 mg every 12 hours. CrCl 50–80: 500 to 1,000 mg every 12 hours (label Table 1).
CrCl 50–80: 500 to 1,000 mg every 12 hours. CrCl 30–50: 250 to 750 mg every 12 hours (label Table 1).
CrCl <30: 250 to 500 mg every 12 hours (label Table 1).
CrCl <30: 250 to 500 mg every 12 hours (label Table 1).

hd.text: ESRD on dialysis: 500 to 1,000 mg every 24 hours, plus a 250 to 500 mg supplemental dose after each dialysis (label Table 1). About 50% removed in a 4-hour session.

pd.text: The label's ESRD-on-dialysis row (500 to 1,000 mg every 24 hours) does not separate PD from HD; the post-dialysis supplement is for hemodialysis. Applying the 24-hour dose to PD without a supplement is clinical extrapolation; specialist input.

crrt.text: No data in label. Removed by dialysis, so CRRT likely clears it; specialist input and seizure monitoring.

dialyzable: Yes: about 50% of the body pool removed in a standard 4-hour hemodialysis (label 10.3, 12.3).
monitoring: Kidney function (CrCl) to set the dose. Seizure control. Behavioral changes, mood, suicidal thinking; somnolence and coordination problems. Avoid abrupt withdrawal.

pediatric.approved_ages: Partial-onset seizures from 1 month; myoclonic seizures 12 years and older; primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures 6 years and older (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Partial-onset: 1 to <6 months, 7 mg/kg twice daily up to 21 mg/kg twice daily; 6 months to <4 years, 10 up to 25 mg/kg twice daily; 4 to <16 years, 10 up to 30 mg/kg twice daily (label 2.2).
pediatric.max_dose: 30 mg/kg twice daily (4 to <16 years); do not exceed adult maximum 3,000 mg/day.

renal.recommendation: The label's kidney dosing table is for adults only; no pediatric kidney dose is given. Clearance falls with CrCl, so reduce by clinical judgment with specialist input.
No pediatric kidney dose in label. Specialist input.
No pediatric kidney dose in label. Specialist input.

hd.text: No pediatric dialysis dose in label; dialyzable (supplement after HD likely needed). Specialist input.

sources.citation: UCB, Inc. (2026). KEPPRA (levetiracetam) tablets and oral solution [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA021505, set ID 3ca9df05-a506-4ec8-a4fe-320f1219ab21, version effective January 28, 2026]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

adult: Key interactions left empty: the label has no drug-interaction section with clinically significant pairs (not CYP-metabolized; under 10% protein-bound).
Site CrCl bands do not match the label's 50/80 cut-offs, so the ≥60 and 30–59 tiles each carry two label rows (amber).
PD tile is extrapolation from the generic 'ESRD patients using dialysis' row (labelled as such).
Injection products (PH 500 mg/5 mL) use the same kidney dosing per the Keppra injection label (not the selected label).
